 "action": "create",
 "name": "arc-marker-guided-mirror",
 "description": "Solve ARC puzzles with a color-4 source and color-6 directional marker; remove the marker and mirror the source as shown by examples.",
 "goal": "Persist the verified transformation rule and examples from this Continual-ARC instance for future similar tasks.",
 "evidence": "Four demo pairs showed color 6 removed and a reflected copy of color 4 added; a fifth test submission using the inverse-T marker orientation placed a horizontal reflection to the left and was confirmed correct.",
 "proposal_content": "# ARC marker-guided mirroring

Use this procedure when an ARC grid contains a color-4 pattern and a separate color-6 marker, and demos show the marker replaced by a copy of the 4-pattern.

1. Separate the 4-pattern from the 6-marker and record each shape's occupied coordinates and bounding box. Preserve the original 4-pattern.
2. Infer the reflection direction from the 6-marker's orientation using the demonstrations: a cross/plus-like marker selected a vertical reflection copied below the source; a T with its bar above its stem selected a horizontal reflection copied to the right; the inverse-T marker (stem above a lower bar) selected a horizontal reflection copied to the left. Treat this as demo-backed for this task family, not as a universal ARC rule.
3. Reflect the source pattern across the corresponding axis and place the reflected cells in the space indicated by the marker. Demos show adjoining/overlapping mirror placements can occur; derive the axis and offset from the source-marker layout rather than simply copying the source at the marker's bounding box.
4. Remove every 6-cell, keep every original 4-cell, add only the reflected 4-cells, and leave all other cells 0. Check the result against all available demo pairs and preserve grid dimensions.

Verified cases from one task: plus-like 6 markers led to a vertical reflected copy below; downward-T markers led to horizontal copies on the right; an inverse-T marker led to a horizontal copy on the left. The inverse-T case was confirmed correct on the test grid. If the marker orientation or placement does not match these examples, request a demo rather than guessing the transform."
}
